sampling_cost_scope: Same number of complete contract paths, different information access: MPS methods use all 100 terminal probabilities, optimized exponential proposals and exact conditional bridge tables. Baselines retain S1 annual probability queries. Finite 2 country exact contraction is already cheaper than this proposal setup. This is classical structural variance reduction, not a black box query or quantum advantage.
proposal_objective: For each of five fixed payoffs minimize log E exp(theta L/160m) plus log E[f^2 exp(-theta L/160m)] for theta in [-20,80], mix equally, use unbiased p/q terminal likelihood weights. All calibration uses the known official model only; replicate errors are not used for proposal selection.
independent_replicates: 32 independent randomizations with seeds 1729 through 1760, nested powers of two within each seed.

scaling.construction: Independent compound Poisson marks plus independent shared group Poisson counts; within each group marks are conditionally independent across countries. Aggregate three year independent increments before the cap. Count at least four folds exactly because every EQ mark is positive. Shared rain count folds exactly to a bit.
scaling.graph_scope: Independent, disjoint pair blocks, nearest neighbor chain and a single global hyperedge. Each selected graph has at most one 10 state latent group crossing a country order cut. General dense pair graphs can require exponentially increasing chi.
scaling.complexity: Core expectation O(n chi^2 d). Exact portfolio polynomial DP adds the loss grid length L=32n+1: O(n chi^2 d L), with global diagonal cores admitting O(n chi d L). Core construction and TT rounding are timed separately.
scaling.year_semigroup: Three year cap equals cap of the three annual sums by independent increments and associativity of capped addition. It is not an uncontrolled cubed latent approximation.
scaling.loss_pmf_truncation: Exact chosen graph cores use no SVD truncation; rounded cores are separate diagnostic approximations and may lose positivity.
